info.name: Apollo B7A6 Housing & Roommate Platform API
info.description:
Versioned backend API for the Housing & Roommate Platform (Node.js + TypeScript + Express + Prisma + Stripe).

Generated from docs/openapi.json by scripts/gen-postman.js (OpenAPI 3.0.3).

HOW TO USE
1. Open the "Demo walkthrough (run in order)" folder and right-click it -> "Run collection".
   That executes requests 0-11 in order and prints a pass/fail report for every assertion.
2. Alternatively, open any single walkthrough request and hit Send: each step asserts its expected
   status, captures what the next step needs, then hands off to the next request automatically.
3. The login requests capture adminToken, ownerToken, tenantToken and refreshToken into the
   collection variables, so every protected request runs without copying tokens by hand.
4. Create/booking/room requests capture propertyId, roomId, bookingId, paymentId and
   imageId automatically, so path parameters never need manual editing.
5. Requests 9 and 10 hit the same endpoint as different roles (403 vs 200) to demonstrate RBAC.
6. Request 8 returns a hosted Stripe checkout URL. Pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
7. The walkthrough is repeatable: step 5 puts the seeded room back to AVAILABLE and step 6
   advances the booking dates on every run, so it stays green however often you run it.

Demo accounts
  admin   admin@housing.local / Admin1234!
  owner   owner@housing.local / Owner1234!
  tenant  tenant@housing.local / Tenant1234!

Set the "baseUrl" collection variable if you need to point this at another environment.

item.name: Demo walkthrough (run in order)
item.description: A self-contained demo that exercises the whole platform. Run 0-11 in order; each request prepares the variables the next one needs. Right-click the folder and choose "Run collection" for a single-click run with a pass/fail report, or press Send on any one step and it asserts, captures and hands off to the next step by itself.

request.description: Confirms the deployment is up. Then run the three login requests that follow.

item.name: 1. Log in as ADMIN
checks: pm.test('admin token type is Bearer', function () { pm.expect(data.tokenType).to.eql('Bearer'); });

request.description: Stores adminToken and refreshToken in the collection variables, so the rest of the collection runs without copying tokens.

exec: pm.test('admin token type is Bearer', function () { pm.expect(data.tokenType).to.eql('Bearer'); });
// /auth/login returns no user object, so take the id and role from the access token claims.

request.description: Seeded property with images, rooms and amenities.

exec: postman.setNextRequest("5. Reset a room to AVAILABLE");

request.description: Required before step 6. Creating a booking flips the room to RESERVED, so without this reset the second run of the walkthrough fails with 400 'Room is not available for booking'.

item.name: 6. Create a booking (tenant)
checks: pm.test('room flipped to RESERVED', function () { pm.expect(data.status).to.eql('PENDING'); });

request.description: Stores bookingId for the steps that follow. The pre-request script moves the booking window forward on every run, so re-running the collection never hits the 409 'Room is already booked for these dates'.

exec: // Advance to a fresh 7-day window on every run. The API rejects an overlapping
// booking with 409 'Room is already booked for these dates', so a fixed window would
// make the second run of this walkthrough fail.
pm.test('room flipped to RESERVED', function () { pm.expect(data.status).to.eql('PENDING'); });

request.description: Runs in a single transaction: booking becomes APPROVED, the room becomes OCCUPIED and a Stripe PaymentIntent is created.
Returns a hosted checkoutUrl. Open it in the browser and pay with card 4242 4242 4242 4242 (no expiry or CVC needed). The webhook then flips the payment to SUCCEEDED.
Same endpoint returns 200 with the admin token and 403 here. That contrast is the RBAC proof.
Platform statistics: users, listings, occupancy, booking funnel, revenue, engagement, top properties.

exec: postman.setNextRequest("11. Health: storage driver and cache backend");

item.name: 11. Health: storage driver and cache backend
checks: pm.test('redis cache active', function () { pm.expect(data.cache && data.cache.backend).to.eql('redis'); });

request.description: Reports storage=cloudinary and cache=redis when both are configured.

exec: pm.test('redis cache active', function () { pm.expect(data.cache && data.cache.backend).to.eql('redis'); });
